entries.originalText: We must not trust every word of others or feeling within ourselves, but cautiously and patiently try the matter, whether it be of God.
entries.modernizedText: We must not trust every word of others or feeling within ourselves, but cautiously and patiently test the matter, to see whether it is of God.

entries.originalText: Unhappily we are so weak that we find it easier to believe and speak evil of others, rather than good.
entries.modernizedText: Unhappily, we are so weak that we find it easier to believe and speak evil of others than good.

entries.originalText: But they that are perfect, do not give ready heed to every news-bearer, for they know man’s weakness that it is prone to evil and unstable in words.
entries.modernizedText: But those who are perfect do not readily listen to every bearer of news, for they know human weakness: it is prone to evil and unstable in words.

entries.originalText: This is great wisdom, not to be hasty in action, or stubborn in our own opinions.
entries.modernizedText: This is great wisdom: not to be hasty in action or stubborn in our own opinions.

entries.originalText: A part of this wisdom also is not to believe every word we hear, nor to tell others all that we hear, even though we believe it.
entries.modernizedText: Part of this wisdom is also not to believe every word we hear, nor to tell others all that we hear, even though we believe it.

entries.originalText: Take counsel with a man who is wise and of a good conscience; and seek to be instructed by one better than thyself, rather than to follow thine own inventions.
entries.modernizedText: Take counsel with a person who is wise and has a good conscience, and seek instruction from someone better than yourself rather than following your own inventions.

entries.originalText: A good life maketh a man wise toward God, and giveth him experience in many things.
entries.modernizedText: A good life makes a person wise toward God and gives him experience in many things.

entries.originalText: The more humble a man is in himself, and the more obedient towards God, the wiser will he be in all things, and the more shall his soul be at peace.
entries.modernizedText: The more humble a person is in himself and the more obedient toward God, the wiser he will be in all things, and the more his soul will be at peace.
